text:
maya (support): Flagging urgent tenant escalation — ACME Inc reports p95->p99 spike since ~08:10 UTC, requests stuck in ingress for 400-1200ms extra. Customer hit timeouts. Can we triage? :warning:
raj (eng-runtime): Looking. Any customer request IDs or sample traces?
maya (support): Provided traces in the ticket — sample req IDs: req_az31, req_az34. They're hitting admission queued state, not retrying.
lee (eng-sre): Saw alerts for ingress-queue-depth on us-west-2 — queue depth backend metric jumped 3x at 08:09. Worker pool CPU for the small-tenant pool saturated.
raj (eng-runtime): Hm. Checking routing logs — those req IDs show "admission:waiting" then a long wait, then 429s from the tenant limiter plugin. Stack shows per-tenant concurrency reached 30 (configured), but overall worker threads are stuck GC-ing?
ana (customer-success): ACME says traffic pattern didn't change. They run bursts of short chat completions.
lee (eng-sre): Pulling worker pod logs now.
deploy-bot: Rolling deploy detected for model-router v2.4.1 at 07:58 UTC.
raj (eng-runtime): That deploy touched the router's fairness scheduler — possible regression in the priority token refill. Might explain sudden per-tenant starvation during bursts.
maya (support): Customer asked for mitigation plan asap — they want traffic unblocked.
lee (eng-sre): Quick mitigation: increase tenant concurrency limit for acme to 60 temporarily, and drain the small-tenant worker pool to force pods to reschedule. Will that cause other tenants to be impacted?
raj (eng-runtime): Increasing tenant concurrency is safe short-term; we should also enable fallback routing to generic-capacity tier so excess requests bypass per-tenant limiter.
nana (customer-success): I'll tell ACME we're applying a temporary concurrency bump + fallback routing, ETA 10m.
maya (support): Please confirm steps so I can update ticket.
lee (eng-sre): Steps I'm running: 1) kubectl patch configmap tenant-limits --patch '{"data":{"acme.concurrency":"60"}}' 2) rollout restart deployment worker-small --field-selector=metadata.name in (worker-small-*) 3) flip routing flag acme:allow-fallback=true in router-config.
raj (eng-runtime): Also running a quick hotfix to revert the priority token change in model-router config: set scheduler.refill_ms back to 200 -> 100. If that doesn't help we'll rollback v2.4.1.
maya (support): Noted. Can we add a safeguard so acme doesn't blow past quota while throttled?
lee (eng-sre): We keep billing quotas separate; temporary concurrency bump is allowed with manual monitoring. I'll add a short-lived alert for acme request rate.
nana (customer-success): ACME confirmed they're seeing improved p95 after ~5min.
raj (eng-runtime): Observability: p95 dropped from 870ms to 120ms for acme path, p99 still ~600ms for some tail requests. Tracing shows fewer "admission:waiting" states.
maya (support): Customer asked for root cause writeup and permanent fix timeline.
raj (eng-runtime): Root cause summary draft: model-router v2.4.1 introduced a change in the fairness scheduler token refill logic that reduced effective priority tokens under bursty short-req workloads. This caused per-tenant admission queues to pile up and worker pools to hit CPU/IO backpressure. Mitigations: revert refill change, add canary tests for bursty short sequences, add a per-tenant emergency fallback to generic capacity with opt-out flag, and expose tenant-level queue depth in console.
lee (eng-sre): We also observed a small memgrowth pattern on worker-small after the router change — will monitor. Possible work-stealing interaction caused context queue retention.
maya (support): Thanks. Customer wants ETA on permanent fix. Can we give a timeline?
raj (eng-runtime): Plan: hot-revert today (PR open, testing now), rollout to canary by EOD, full rollback if canary passes tomorrow morning. Permanent fix (robust refill + unit tests + load test) targeted next sprint (2 weeks).
nana (customer-success): Sharing timeline with ACME. They're ok with temporary measures and want the rollback prioritized.
maya (support): Closing loop — ACME confirmed no more timeouts after measures; will keep monitoring.
lee (eng-sre): I'll leave an after-action note and add a short runbook step: if queue depth>X and p99>Y then enable tenant fallback and raise page.
raj (eng-runtime): Added a quick dashboard panel to show per-tenant queued_requests and refill_rate; sending link.
maya (support): Thanks team. Marking as resolved for now, will reopen if regressions recur. :white_check_mark:
